newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Capital pours scorn on London bid.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Capital pours scorn on London bid.

text.p: British gaming company Capital Corp Plc stressed again on Tuesday that a hostile bid by London Clubs International undervalued the firm. "The offer in no way recognises any of our strengths. It is completely unacceptable, derisory, illogical and we firmly reject it," chairman Garry Nesbitt told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Capital is sending its offer response to shareholders today and points out that the bid represents a discount of 10.5 percent to its 213p per share closing price on Monday.
By 1230 GMT, shares in Capital had fallen three pence to stand at 210p.
The firm also unveiled results for 1996 as part of its response to the takeover bid. London launched the 181 million pounds all paper offer on February 17.
Pre-tax profits at the casino operator slipped to 9.2 million stg after an exceptional charge of 2.8 million from 13.1 million previously.
It said that a lower volume of high rollers, particularly at the tail-end of last year, and a lower overall win percentage in the second half had had a negative impact on results.
"We are making noises about the fact that the high rollers have returned in the first quarter of this year, so we consider that (the tail end of last year) was cyclical," said Nesbitt.

"This is the first year that we have had two clubs up and running and the profit flowing from both of them, without the prospect of exceptional costs, so we are quite confident about the prospects for 1997," he added.
Capital, with around a 20 percent share of the London market, operates Crockfords and the Colony Club, which was opened last year.
Alan Goodenough, chief executive of suitor London Clubs, said in response to Capital's latest results, "It must be a sad day for shareholders to see that nothing has really changed at Capital Corp."
"The best they can do is say that the year started well, just what they said in March '94, '95 and '96. The evential outcome for those years was a profit fall in each. Need I say more."
